plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine that produces dramatic cascading clusters of fragrant, pea-like flowers. It can twine over pergolas, walls, and trees, and its blooms appear before or alongside the emerging leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to China; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across Europe, Japan, and North America
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines can live for over a century, and some famous specimens, like the one in Sierra Madre, California, cover more than an acre.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above blue-green foliage. Late-season varieties are at their peak in late April, filling parks and fields with bands of color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to early May)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; famous displays in the Netherlands, Turkey, and the Skagit Valley in Washington, USA
plants.funFact: During the 1630s Dutch Tulip Mania, a single rare bulb could sell for more than the price of a luxurious canal house.

plants.name: Cornus florida
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose showy display comes from four large petal-like bracts surrounding a tight cluster of tiny true flowers. It lights up woodland edges and suburban yards in the eastern United States.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May)
plants.location: Eastern North America, from southern Ontario to Florida and west to Texas
plants.funFact: The bright red berries that follow the bloom are an important autumn food source for songbirds and other wildlife.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A graceful semi-deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into masses of trumpet-shaped purple-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere it is finishing its autumn-to-spring cycle, while in the tropics and subtropics some trees bloom in spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (April to June); late spring in South America's northern ranges
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); cultivated in Mexico, Southern California, Florida, and parts of Asia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, tens of thousands of jacarandas line the streets, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.
